chapter: A musical family and the old New Orleans bands
title: Cousin Estee Bijou, the Creole Songbird
summary: Danny's cousin Estee Bijou was a vaudeville star whose husband Irving C. Miller said she nagged him.

story.theme_name: Meeting, marrying and raising a family
story.community_name: Meeting, courting and marrying: musicians' love lives

blocks.x: And I had a cousin, Estee Bijou, and you mentioned relatives...

She was a star. She was Irving C. Miller's wife. She was a very beautiful Creole woman. I have a picture of her at the house, and you can see. and she was a star. They called her The Creole Songbird. So I saw Irving C. Miller about 1940 in New York, and I asked him about Estee Bijou, his relationship. He said she was wonderful, a beautiful woman, but she was a little off in her head. He said, "She nagged me. I couldn't sleep. She nagged me, accusing me of winning all the time. And the other thing with ...(?)..., she'd call and disturb me. She was superstitious. And I couldn't stand it no longer. I had to let it go."
